description: En la mitología griega, Artemisa y Ares compartían el Olimpo. Hoy, sus nombres se encuentran nuevamente en una nueva frontera: Marte. Inspirados por esta conexión y el espíritu explorador de Artemisa, somos Artemis's Gems, un equipo impulsado por la curiosidad científica, la innovación y la colaboración. Buscamos transformar el conocimiento en soluciones que contribuyan al futuro de la exploración espacial y cruzar fronteras hacia lo desconocido.
summary: MARSWALK is a mission tablet that helps astronauts plan and rehearse a walk on Mars. Set in Gale Crater, it layers multiple views of the terrain built from NASA data, highlights hazards and shelters, and helps plot safer routes while tracking the astronaut’s suit status. A rover partner, Artemis, works alongside the crew, and a simulation mode lets them rehearse under changing conditions before they go. It addresses the challenge by turning regional Mars data into a hyperlocal, layered view for a single excursion, with safety and science at its core. It matters because the first human steps on Mars will demand decisions at the scale of meters, and MARSWALK helps ensure the first Marswalk is rehearsed, not improvised.
details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works

MARSWALK is a mission tablet for planning and rehearsing a Marswalk in Gale Crater, near the boxwork formations of Mount Sharp. It layers six views of the terrain (optical, topographic, thermal, spectral, radiation, and dust), built from NASA data (JPL Mars Trek and USGS), with hazard zones, shelters, and mineral veins annotated with safety checks and source references. Users plot Safest or Fastest Risk routes while a suit panel tracks heart rate, oxygen, hydration, energy, and radiation dose. They can switch between the astronaut, Artemis (a rover sintered from local regolith), or split control. A simulation mode lets crews rehearse the same route under calm, windy, or storm conditions, including crisis and rescue scenarios.

Benefits:

Turns regional Mars data into a hyperlocal view for a single excursion.

Puts hazards, shelters, radiation, and suit status in one place, so route decisions are informed by safety.

Lets crews rehearse before they go, which reduces improvisation and risk.

Expected impact:

Human missions to Mars will require decisions at the scale of meters. MARSWALK aims to support the planning and training of future surface excursions and to complement existing EVA planning tools. It can also help educators and the public understand what a real Marswalk involves.

Tools and technologies:

We built MARSWALK as an interactive web app using Google AI Studio and Gemini to accelerate development, running in the browser on laptops and phones. Terrain and mission context are generated from NASA Gale Crater data (JPL Mars Trek and USGS), with site information based on findings from MSL Curiosity and MRO HiRISE.

Creativity:

-A rover partner, Artemis, built from local regolith, with astronaut, rover, and split control.

-A rehearsal mode with weather and crisis events, so the map becomes a training environment and not just a display.

-A suit panel connected to route decisions, so each choice has a visible cost.

Factors our team considered:

-Safety first: radiation, slopes, hazard zones, and a return-to-habitat reserve.

-Scientific honesty: we clearly separate what is derived from NASA data from what is simulated for training.

-Usability: simple controls, a built-in tutorial, and a layout meant for a tablet or visor.

-Complementarity: we designed MARSWALK to work alongside existing NASA EVA tools, not replace them.

-Scalability: the same structure can support other locations and data layers in the future.
